class mptorch.quant.mac.BlockMac(a, b=None, acc=None, *, fused=False, rounding=RoundMode.RNE, accumulate_algorithm=AccumulateAlgorithm.NAIVE, carrier=None, block_size=None, outer=None, tensor_scale_epilogue=False)[source]#

The block GEMM: two block-format operands and the arithmetic of their product.

a and b are the formats that the left and right operands are packed in. Each is a mptorch.BlockFormat (packed to nearest even) or a BlockQuant (which specifies the rounding and a tensor scale). b defaults to a.

The product decodes both operands in the carrier and sums their products as mptorch.quant.block_matmul() describes. In a split mac, each product is rounded to the carrier and the sum to acc. With fused=True, each fused multiply-add is rounded to acc. acc=None leaves the sum in the carrier. The accumulate algorithms are those of SplitMac.

mptorch.quant.qmatmul() and mptorch.quant.QMatmul accept a BlockMac (mptorch.quant.block_matmul_formats() builds their formats). They also accept a bare BlockFormat, which means BlockMac(fmt).

Parameters:

  • a (BlockFormat | BlockQuant) – the left operand’s format.

  • b (BlockFormat | BlockQuant | None) – the right operand’s. Default: None, a’s.

  • acc (BinaryK | None) – the accumulate format. Default: None

  • fused (bool) – a fused multiply-add per step. Default: False

  • rounding (RoundMode) – the sum’s rounding mode. Default: RoundMode.RNE

  • accumulate_algorithm (AccumulateAlgorithm) – as for SplitMac (TREE needs fused=False). Default: AccumulateAlgorithm.NAIVE

  • carrier (dtype | None) – torch.float64 packs the operands and multiplies them in binary64, whatever their dtype (an operand BlockQuant that names a carrier of its own keeps it). Default: None, the operands’: binary64 for float64 tensors, binary32 otherwise.

  • block_size (int | None) – as for SplitMac. Default: None

  • outer (BinaryK | None) – as for SplitMac. Default: None

  • tensor_scale_epilogue (bool) – apply the operands’ per-tensor scales once, to the result, as NVIDIA’s NVFP4 GEMMs do, instead of in each decoded element (mptorch.quant.block_matmul()). Default: False

Example:

>>> import torch
>>> from mptorch import BinaryK, MXFP8_E4M3, MXFP4_E2M1
>>> from mptorch.quant import BlockMac, qmm
>>> mac = BlockMac(MXFP8_E4M3, MXFP4_E2M1, BinaryK(16, 11))
>>> qmm(torch.randn(4, 64), torch.randn(64, 8), mac).shape
torch.Size([4, 8])

Matrix products#

The differentiable matmul entry points: qmm, qbmm and qmatmul.

These are the functions to reach for. The eight *_matmul* wrappers in mptorch.quant.ops are the schema-faithful tier, one function per op with every schema argument spelled out and no autograd; these sit above them, taking a format object instead of twenty integers and carrying a gradient.

formats accepts, in increasing order of specificity:

  • None: plain torch.matmul, which is what an A/B against unquantized arithmetic wants;

  • a Number (BinaryK(8, 4)): shorthand for SplitMac(mul=fmt, acc=fmt), the common case where one format is used for both halves of the dot product, and for a BlockFormat, BlockMac(fmt): both operands packed in it, the sum in binary32;

  • a BlockMac: two packed block-format operands and the arithmetic of their product (mptorch.quant.block_matmul_formats());

  • a SplitMac / FusedMac: the dot-product arithmetic, with a palette in any slot selecting the per-output-element op and requiring prec_idx, and a carrier choosing the float arithmetic it is computed in (binary64 for any operands with torch.float64, never narrower than theirs);

  • a QMatmulFormats: per-pass arithmetic and operand quantizers, that is, everything the layer can vary.

The first three are resolved (and memoized) into the fourth, so there is one implementation and one thing to test.

mptorch.quant.matmul.qmm(a, b, formats=None, *, prec_idx=None)[source]#

qmatmul() restricted to two matrices, as torch.mm is.

Parameters:

  • a (Tensor) – a [M, K] matrix.

  • b (Tensor) – a [K, N] matrix of the same dtype.

  • formats (Any) – as for qmatmul(). Default: None

  • prec_idx (Tensor | None) – as for qmatmul(). Default: None

Returns:

the [M, N] product.

Return type:

Tensor

Raises:

ValueError – if either operand is not 2D, plus qmatmul()’s.

Example:

>>> import torch
>>> from mptorch import BinaryK
>>> from mptorch.quant import qmm
>>> qmm(torch.randn(4, 8), torch.randn(8, 3), BinaryK(8, 4)).shape
torch.Size([4, 3])

There is no broadcasting: both batch dimensions must be equal. torch.bmm makes this check and qmatmul does not.

Parameters:

  • a (Tensor) – a [B, M, K] batch of matrices.

  • b (Tensor) – a [B, K, N] batch of the same dtype.

  • formats (Any) – as for qmatmul(). Default: None

  • prec_idx (Tensor | None) – as for qmatmul(). Default: None

Returns:

the [B, M, N] batch of products.

Return type:

Tensor

Raises:

ValueError – if either operand is not 3D or the batch sizes differ, plus qmatmul()’s.

Example:

>>> import torch
>>> from mptorch import BinaryK
>>> from mptorch.quant import FusedMac, qbmm
>>> a, b = torch.randn(2, 4, 8), torch.randn(2, 8, 3)
>>> qbmm(a, b, FusedMac(BinaryK(8, 4))).shape

mptorch.quant.matmul.qmatmul(a, b, formats=None, *, prec_idx=None)[source]#

torch.matmul’s contract, computed in the arithmetic formats names.

It accepts everything torch.matmul accepts: 1D promotion on either operand, and leading dimensions of any rank broadcast against each other. It is differentiable in both operands, and each gradient is computed in the arithmetic of its own hook. Float64 operands are computed in binary64. The others are computed in binary32, unless a mac’s carrier asks for binary64. In both cases each pass checks the formats against its carrier and warns (mptorch.FormatRangeWarning) about what the carrier cannot hold.

Two shapes need no copy:

  • An operand that is the transpose of a contiguous tensor (q @ k.mT) sets the kernel’s transpose flag and is not materialized.

  • [..., M, K] @ [K, N] folds its batch into M, giving one large GEMM instead of a batch of small ones.

Both are bit-identical to the batched spelling, stochastic rounding included, because each output element’s random stream is keyed on its index into the output.

Parameters:

  • a (Tensor) – the left operand, 1D or higher.

  • b (Tensor) – the right operand, 1D or higher, of the same dtype.

  • formats (Any) – the arithmetic. The module docstring says what each spelling means. Default: None (plain torch.matmul)

  • prec_idx (Tensor | None) – an integer map of the forward pass’s output shape ([M, N], [M, 1] or [1, N], optionally batched) that selects a palette entry per output element. It is required by a palette format and by nothing else. It is the forward’s map. A palette that also has to differentiate needs one map per pass; use the agrad_prec_idx and bgrad_prec_idx arguments of mptorch.quant.matmul_formats() for those. Default: None

Returns:

a @ b in the operands’ dtype, with torch.matmul’s output shape.

Return type:

Tensor

Raises:

  • ValueError – for a palette without prec_idx, a prec_idx with no palette, or a carrier narrower than the operands.

  • TypeError – for a formats value of another type.

Example:

>>> import torch
>>> from mptorch import BinaryK
>>> from mptorch.quant import SplitMac, qmatmul
>>> a, b = torch.randn(5, 2, 4, 8), torch.randn(8, 3)
>>> qmatmul(a, b, BinaryK(8, 4)).shape
torch.Size([5, 2, 4, 3])
>>> qmatmul(a, b, SplitMac(BinaryK(8, 4), acc=None)).shape
torch.Size([5, 2, 4, 3])
mptorch.quant.matmul.as_matmul_formats(formats, prec_idx=None)[source]#

Normalize whatever a caller passed as formats to a QMatmulFormats.

The four spellings listed in the module docstring are told apart here and nowhere else, so qmatmul() and mptorch.quant.QMatmul accept exactly the same values.

Parameters:

  • formats (Any) – the arithmetic, in any of the accepted spellings.

  • prec_idx (Tensor | None) – the forward’s palette map, for a SplitMac/FusedMac holding a palette. Default: None

Returns:

formats itself if it already was one, an empty QMatmulFormats() for None, or the memoized one for a mac.

Return type:

QMatmulFormats

Raises:

  • ValueError – for a prec_idx given with None (nothing to select from) or with a QMatmulFormats (whose maps were bound by mptorch.quant.matmul_formats()).

  • TypeError – for any other formats value.

class mptorch.quant.QMatmulFormats(a_quant=None, b_quant=None, agrad_quant=None, bgrad_quant=None, fwd_math=None, bwd_agrad_math=None, bwd_bgrad_math=None, recompute_a=None, recompute_b=None)[source]#

Quantizers and custom math for a quantized matmul.

QMatmul and mptorch.quant.qmatmul() read this container. Its slots mirror those of QAffineFormats, renamed for an op whose two operands play the same role: a/b instead of input/weight, and one gradient quantizer per operand, because the two gradient GEMMs may need different formats. Every slot is optional, and None means plain PyTorch. A QMatmulFormats() with nothing set computes torch.matmul and its ordinary gradients.

There is no output_quant, on purpose. Rounding the result of the op is an elementwise step, so the caller applies a quantizer for it; it is not a slot on every op’s formats.

The class inherits from nn.Module, which registers a stateful quantizer (a QAT observer) in the parent model’s state_dict.

The recompute_* flags are QAffineFormats’ for the two operands: keep a (b) raw for backward and quantize it again there, instead of keeping a quantized copy. Both default to keeping the copy, since a matmul’s operands are activations and whether anything else keeps one alive depends on the model.

Parameters:

  • a_quant (Callable | None) – applied to a in the forward. Default: None

  • b_quant (Callable | None) – applied to b in the forward. Default: None

  • agrad_quant (Callable | None) – applied to the output gradient before a’s gradient GEMM. Default: None

  • bgrad_quant (Callable | None) – applied to the output gradient before b’s gradient GEMM. Default: None

  • fwd_math (Callable | None) – fwd_math(q_a, q_b) -> a @ b. Default: None

  • bwd_agrad_math (Callable | None) – bwd_agrad_math(q_grad, q_b) -> grad @ b^T. Default: None

  • bwd_bgrad_math (Callable | None) – bwd_bgrad_math(q_grad, q_a) -> a^T @ grad. Default: None

  • recompute_a (bool | None) – keep a raw for backward and run a_quant on it again there. None keeps the copy. Set it where something else keeps a alive, as attention’s softmax keeps the probabilities that multiply V. True runs any callable again, as for QAffineFormats. Default: None

  • recompute_b (bool | None) – the same for b and b_quant. Default: None

Example:

>>> from mptorch import BinaryK
>>> from mptorch.quant import QMatmul, Quant, SplitMac, matmul_formats
>>> formats = matmul_formats(SplitMac(BinaryK(8, 4), BinaryK(16, 11)))
>>> formats.a_quant = Quant(BinaryK(8, 4))
>>> formats.b_quant = Quant(BinaryK(8, 4))
>>> attn = QMatmul(formats)

Initialize internal Module state, shared by both nn.Module and ScriptModule.

class mptorch.quant.QMatmul(formats=None)[source]#

torch.matmul with the arithmetic of one QMatmulFormats.

This is the module form of mptorch.quant.qmatmul(). Like QLinear, it is a module because its formats are one: a QMatmulFormats is an nn.Module, so a quantizer that carries state (a QAT observer) is registered in the parent model’s state_dict when the matmul is held as a submodule. A quantized attention block calls two of these per head. For backward it keeps quantized copies of both operands, unless the formats’ recompute_a / recompute_b say to keep an operand raw and quantize it again there (worth it for the softmax probabilities, which softmax keeps alive anyway).

Parameters:

formats (None or Number or SplitMac or FusedMac or QMatmulFormats) – everything mptorch.quant.qmatmul() accepts, converted once here by mptorch.quant.matmul.as_matmul_formats(). Default: None (plain torch.matmul)

Shape:

  • Input: a and b in any shapes torch.matmul accepts.

  • Output: torch.matmul’s output shape.

Example:

>>> import torch
>>> from mptorch import BinaryK
>>> from mptorch.quant import QMatmul, SplitMac
>>> mm = QMatmul(SplitMac(BinaryK(8, 4), BinaryK(16, 11)))
>>> mm(torch.randn(2, 4, 8), torch.randn(8, 3)).shape
torch.Size([2, 4, 3])

mptorch.quant.matmul_formats(mac, *, prec_idx=None, agrad_prec_idx=None, bgrad_prec_idx=None)[source]#

Build a QMatmulFormats whose three passes run in mac’s arithmetic.

The forward product a @ b, a’s gradient grad @ b^T and b’s gradient a^T @ grad each run through the GEMM op that mac resolves to.

A palette in any of mac’s slots selects the per-output-element op, which needs one prec_idx map per pass. The maps are bound into the hooks here instead of being passed through every call. A gradient pass whose map is missing raises when it is reached; it does not fall back to unquantized arithmetic.

Like the four *_gemm_formats factories, this sets only the math hooks. The caller adds elementwise operand quantization (a_quant, b_quant, agrad_quant, bgrad_quant) separately.

Parameters:

  • mac (SplitMac | FusedMac) – the dot-product arithmetic, resolved once through mptorch.quant.mac.spec_for_mac().

  • prec_idx (Tensor | None) – integer map selecting a palette entry per element of the forward’s output, shaped like a @ b ([M, N], [M, 1] or [1, N], optionally batched). Required by, and only by, a palette mac. Default: None

  • agrad_prec_idx (Tensor | None) – the map for a’s gradient, shaped like grad @ b^T. Default: None

  • bgrad_prec_idx (Tensor | None) – the map for b’s gradient, shaped like a^T @ grad. Default: None

Returns:

with fwd_math, bwd_agrad_math and bwd_bgrad_math set and every *_quant slot left None.

Return type:

QMatmulFormats

Raises:

ValueError – if mac holds a palette and prec_idx is None, or if a map is given for a mac with no palette to select from.

Example:

>>> import torch
>>> from mptorch import BinaryK
>>> from mptorch.quant import Palette, QMatmul, SplitMac, matmul_formats
>>> palette = Palette([BinaryK(8, 4), BinaryK(8, 5)])
>>> prec_idx = torch.zeros(4, 3, dtype=torch.int64)
>>> formats = matmul_formats(SplitMac(palette, palette), prec_idx=prec_idx)
>>> QMatmul(formats)(torch.randn(4, 8), torch.randn(8, 3)).shape
torch.Size([4, 3])
mptorch.quant.block_matmul(a, b, *, acc=None, fused=False, rounding=RoundMode.RNE, accumulate_algorithm=AccumulateAlgorithm.NAIVE, block_size=None, outer=None, carrier=None, tensor_scale_epilogue=False)[source]#

Multiply two block-format tensors: a @ b of their logical values.

a is logically [..., M, K] and b is [..., K, N]. The kernel decodes each element as it loads it (its value times its block’s scale, as block_unpack() would) and multiplies in the carrier: binary64 when carrier=torch.float64 or either operand was packed in binary64 (from a float64 tensor, or with that carrier), and binary32 otherwise. A split mac (fused=False) rounds each product to the carrier and the running sum to acc. A fused mac rounds each fused multiply-add to acc. acc=None leaves the sum in the carrier.

Each operand is read along K. It may be packed along its K (a along its last axis, b along its second-to-last) or along its other dimension, which the kernel reads transposed. One packed weight therefore serves both x @ w.T and g @ w; BlockPacked.mT is the transpose, without a copy. The two operands may have different formats. Leading dimensions must be equal, or absent on one side. The function is not differentiable: see mptorch.quant.qmatmul() with a mptorch.quant.BlockMac.

A format with a per-tensor scale (NVFP4’s E4M3, or a superfp scale) decodes each element as its value times its block’s scale times the tensor scale, inside the loop. tensor_scale_epilogue=True does what NVIDIA’s NVFP4 GEMMs do instead. The loop sees the elements times their block scales only, and the result is multiplied once by the product of the two tensor scales, rounded to the carrier. The two agree in exact arithmetic and round differently. In the second, the accumulate format sees products that the tensor scales have not scaled, so it needs their range.

Parameters:

  • a (BlockPacked) – the left operand.

  • b (BlockPacked) – the right operand.

  • acc (BinaryK | None) – the accumulate format. Default: None

  • fused (bool) – one rounding per step (a fused multiply-add) instead of two. Default: False

  • rounding (RoundMode) – the rounding mode of the sum. Default: RoundMode.RNE

  • accumulate_algorithm (AccumulateAlgorithm) – as for mptorch.quant.SplitMac. Default: AccumulateAlgorithm.NAIVE

  • block_size (int | None) – BLOCK’s and TREE’s block size. Default: None

  • outer (BinaryK | None) – BLOCK’s and TREE’s outer format. Default: None

  • carrier (dtype | None) – torch.float64 multiplies in binary64; torch.float32 refuses an operand packed in binary64. Default: None, the operands’ carrier.

  • tensor_scale_epilogue (bool) – apply the operands’ tensor scales to the result instead of in the decode. It has no effect on formats without a tensor scale (E8M0). Default: False

Returns:

[..., M, N], float32 in binary32 and float64 in binary64.

Return type:

Tensor

Example:

>>> import torch
>>> from mptorch import BinaryK, MXFP8_E4M3
>>> from mptorch.quant import block_matmul, block_pack
>>> x, w = torch.randn(4, 64), torch.randn(16, 64)
>>> y = block_matmul(block_pack(x, MXFP8_E4M3), block_pack(w, MXFP8_E4M3).mT,
...                  acc=BinaryK(16, 11))
>>> y.shape
torch.Size([4, 16])
mptorch.quant.block_matmul_formats(mac, *, agrad_mac=None, bgrad_mac=None)[source]#

Build a QMatmulFormats whose three passes are block GEMMs.

Each pass packs its operands along the dimension it sums over:

  • The forward product a @ b packs a along its last dimension and b along its second-to-last (their K), in mac’s two formats.

  • a’s gradient grad @ b^T packs grad along its last dimension and b along its last.

  • b’s gradient a^T @ grad packs a along its second-to-last dimension and grad along its second-to-last.

A gradient pass takes the formats of the slots it fills from agrad_mac / bgrad_mac, which default to mac. An operand whose format has square tiles is packed once, by the a_quant / b_quant slot that this function sets for it. The gradient passes read that packing through mptorch.quant.BlockPacked.mT. Each pass’s result is in the carrier (float32, or float64 in binary64), stored in the operands’ dtype.

Parameters:

  • mac (BlockMac) – the forward’s operand formats and arithmetic.

  • agrad_mac (BlockMac | None) – a’s gradient’s. Default: None

  • bgrad_mac (BlockMac | None) – b’s gradient’s. Default: None

Returns:

the three math hooks, and a_quant / b_quant for square-tiled operands.

Return type:

QMatmulFormats

Example:

>>> import torch
>>> from mptorch import BinaryK, MXFP8_E4M3
>>> from mptorch.quant import BlockMac, QMatmul, block_matmul_formats
>>> layer = QMatmul(block_matmul_formats(BlockMac(MXFP8_E4M3, acc=BinaryK(16, 11))))
>>> layer(torch.randn(4, 64), torch.randn(64, 8)).shape
torch.Size([4, 8])

The schema tier#

One function per kernel, with every schema argument spelled out and no autograd. See Calling the kernels for when to use these instead of qmatmul.

mptorch.quant.binaryK_matmul(a, b, *, trans_a=False, trans_b=False, mul_K, mul_P, mul_bias=None, mul_is_signed=True, mul_prng_bits=0, accumulate_quant=True, acc_K=None, acc_P=None, acc_bias=None, acc_is_signed=None, acc_prng_bits=0, accumulate_algorithm=AccumulateAlgorithm.NAIVE, rounding_mode=RoundMode.RNE, saturation_mode=SaturationMode.SAT_NONE, subnormals_mode=SubnormalsMode.SUBNORMALS, acc_saturation_mode=None, acc_subnormals_mode=None, block_size=None, outer_K=None, outer_P=None, outer_bias=None, outer_is_signed=None, outer_prng_bits=0, outer_saturation_mode=None, outer_subnormals_mode=None, carrier=None, carrier_rounding=RoundMode.RNE)[source]#

Quantized GEMM with a split multiply-accumulate in binaryK formats.

Computes op(a) @ op(b), where op(x) = x.T when the corresponding trans_* flag is set, and op(x) = x otherwise. This is not the same as quantizing a and b and then calling torch.matmul. It quantizes the arithmetic of each dot product. Every partial product is rounded to the binaryK format given by mul_K/mul_P. When accumulate_quant is true, the running sum is rounded to the format given by acc_K/acc_P after every accumulation step. With accumulate_quant=False the running sum stays at the carrier’s precision and only the multiply is quantized.

Everything the formats do not round (a product or a sum before its rounding) is computed in a carrier, and so are the roundings. The carrier is binary64 for float64 operands and binary32 for float32, float16 and bfloat16. Every call checks both formats against that carrier. The result holds the accumulate format’s values, so that format is also checked against a result dtype narrower than the carrier, as in binaryK_quantize().

a and b follow torch.matmul’s operand rules: 1D operands are promoted (and their dimension is dropped from the result), leading dimensions broadcast against each other, and trans_a/trans_b apply to the last two dimensions. Three cases need no copy:

  • A shared operand is read at stride 0 instead of being expanded.

  • An operand that is the transpose of a contiguous tensor flips the kernel’s flag instead of being copied.

  • [..., M, K] @ [K, N] folds its batch into M as a view.

The two shapes that a quantized attention block uses are covered by these. Under RoundMode.SR each output element’s random stream is keyed on its index into the [batch, M, N] result, so the folded and the batched spellings are bit-identical.

This function resolves the format on every call. A caller that keeps one format across many calls should use the factories of mptorch.quant.gemm, which resolve it once per layer. mptorch.quant.qmatmul() is the differentiable entry point.

Parameters:

  • a (Tensor) – the left operand; float32, float64, float16 or bfloat16.

  • b (Tensor) – the right operand, of a’s dtype and device.

  • trans_a (bool) – read a transposed in its last two dimensions. Default: False

  • trans_b (bool) – read b transposed in its last two dimensions. Default: False

  • mul_K (int) – width in bits of the multiply format.

  • mul_P (int) – precision of the multiply format.

  • mul_bias (int | None) – exponent bias of the multiply format. Default: None, P3109’s 2**(K - P - 1) signed and 2**(K - P) unsigned.

  • mul_is_signed (bool) – whether the multiply format has a sign bit. Default: True

  • mul_prng_bits (int) – random bits RoundMode.SR draws for the multiply rounding, as binaryK_quantize()’s prng_bits. Default: 0

  • accumulate_quant (bool) – whether the running sum is rounded to the accumulate format after every step. Default: True

  • acc_K (int | None) – width of the accumulate format. Default: None, mul_K.

  • acc_P (int | None) – precision of the accumulate format. Default: None, mul_P.

  • acc_bias (int | None) – exponent bias of the accumulate format. Default: None, P3109’s for acc_K/acc_P.

  • acc_is_signed (bool | None) – whether the accumulate format has a sign bit. Default: None, mul_is_signed.

  • acc_prng_bits (int) – random bits RoundMode.SR draws for the accumulate rounding. Default: 0

  • accumulate_algorithm (AccumulateAlgorithm) – how the products are summed. NAIVE is the step above, in order. KAHAN carries a compensation term next to the sum, rounded to the accumulate format. BLOCK runs the step above over blocks of block_size products and adds each block’s sum to a total, which the outer format rounds. TREE sums each block’s products pairwise, rounding every pair’s sum to the accumulate format, and adds the block’s root to the total in the same way. mptorch.AccumulateAlgorithm states each precisely. Default: AccumulateAlgorithm.NAIVE

  • rounding_mode (RoundMode) – the rounding of both formats. There is one mode per op, because the kernel is instantiated on it. Default: RoundMode.RNE

  • saturation_mode (SaturationMode) – the multiply format’s overflow behavior. Default: SaturationMode.SAT_NONE

  • subnormals_mode (SubnormalsMode) – the multiply format’s bottom of range. Default: SubnormalsMode.SUBNORMALS

  • acc_saturation_mode (SaturationMode | None) – the accumulate format’s overflow behavior. Default: None, saturation_mode.

  • acc_subnormals_mode (SubnormalsMode | None) – the accumulate format’s bottom of range. Default: None, subnormals_mode.

  • block_size (int | None) – products per block. BLOCK requires one, which must divide 16 or be a multiple of 16 (the kernels count in slabs of 16 steps). TREE takes a power of two in [2, 256] and defaults to 16. NAIVE and KAHAN take none. Default: None

  • outer_K (int | None) – width of the outer format. This is the rounding that BLOCK and TREE apply to the total after each block is added. None (with outer_P) leaves the total in the carrier’s precision. When given, it is the format whose values the result holds, and the one checked against a narrower result dtype. Default: None

  • outer_P (int | None) – precision of the outer format; given together with outer_K. Default: None

  • outer_bias (int | None) – exponent bias of the outer format. Default: None, P3109’s for outer_K/outer_P.

  • outer_is_signed (bool | None) – whether the outer format has a sign bit. Default: None, the accumulate format’s.

  • outer_prng_bits (int) – random bits RoundMode.SR draws for the outer rounding. Default: 0

  • outer_saturation_mode (SaturationMode | None) – the outer format’s overflow behavior. Default: None, the accumulate format’s.

  • outer_subnormals_mode (SubnormalsMode | None) – the outer format’s bottom of range. Default: None, the accumulate format’s.

  • carrier (dtype | None) – as for binaryK_quantize(). torch.float64 widens narrower operands to binary64 and narrows the result back to their dtype with one rounding. torch.float32 refuses float64 operands. Default: None, the operands’ own carrier.

  • carrier_rounding (RoundMode) – how the carrier rounds each product and sum before the formats do. RoundMode.RNE is the carrier’s nearest multiply and add, which the directed modes can then round to the wrong neighbour. RoundMode.RO rounds them to odd, so each format rounds the exact product and the exact sum, for formats with P at most 22 under RNE/RNA, 23 under the directed modes and RO, and P + prng_bits at most 23 under SR in binary32 (51, 52 and 52 in binary64); a call outside those raises. RO runs the custom_matmul_*_odd ops: NAIVE only, on CPU and CUDA tensors. With accumulate_quant=False only the product is rounded to odd. See Dot-product arithmetic, “What the carrier rounds”. Default: RoundMode.RNE

Returns:

the product, in the operands’ dtype, with the shape torch.matmul would give.

Return type:

Tensor

Raises:

  • ValueError – if a carrier cannot hold a format (as for binaryK_quantize()), if carrier names no carrier or is narrower than the operands, or if the operands’ leading dimensions do not broadcast.

  • TypeError – if carrier is neither a torch.dtype nor None.

  • RuntimeError – if the inner dimensions do not match, the operands differ in dtype or device, or an operand requires grad under grad mode (use mptorch.quant.qmatmul()).

Warns:

FormatRangeWarning – if a format’s range exceeds the carrier’s, or the accumulate format’s range reaches past a narrower result dtype’s.

Example:

>>> a = torch.tensor([[1.0, 2.0], [3.0, 4.0]])
>>> binaryK_matmul(a, a, mul_K=8, mul_P=4)
tensor([[ 7., 10.],
        [15., 22.]])
>>> binaryK_matmul(a, a, mul_K=8, mul_P=3)
tensor([[ 7., 10.],
        [16., 24.]])

With three stored mantissa bits (P=4) every product and sum is exact. With two (P=3) the sums 15 and 22 are rounded to 16 and 24.

Quantized GEMM with a split multiply-accumulate in superfp formats.

The superfp analog of binaryK_matmul(). Every partial product is rounded to the superfp format given by mul_man_bits, mul_exp_bits, mul_normal_binades and mul_bias. When accumulate_quant is true, the running sum is rounded to the acc_* format after every step. binaryK_matmul() describes the general contract: torch.matmul’s operand rules, the transpose flags, the carrier, the storage check and the per-call resolution. superfp_quantize() describes the format.

Parameters:

  • a (Tensor) – the left operand; float32, float64, float16 or bfloat16.

  • b (Tensor) – the right operand, of a’s dtype and device.

  • trans_a (bool) – read a transposed in its last two dimensions. Default: False

  • trans_b (bool) – read b transposed in its last two dimensions. Default: False

  • mul_man_bits (int) – stored mantissa bits of the multiply format.

  • mul_exp_bits (int) – exponent bits of the multiply format.

  • mul_normal_binades (int) – binades of the multiply format that carry the mantissa.

  • mul_bias (int) – exponent bias of the multiply format.

  • mul_is_signed (bool) – whether the multiply format has a sign bit. Default: True

  • mul_prng_bits (int) – random bits RoundMode.SR draws for the multiply rounding. Default: 0

  • accumulate_quant (bool) – whether the running sum is rounded to the accumulate format after every step. Default: True

  • acc_man_bits (int | None) – the accumulate format’s mantissa bits. Default: None, mul_man_bits.

  • acc_exp_bits (int | None) – the accumulate format’s exponent bits. Default: None, mul_exp_bits.

  • acc_normal_binades (int | None) – the accumulate format’s normal binades. Default: None, mul_normal_binades.

  • acc_bias (int | None) – the accumulate format’s exponent bias. Default: None, mul_bias.

  • acc_is_signed (bool | None) – whether the accumulate format has a sign bit. Default: None, mul_is_signed.

  • acc_prng_bits (int) – random bits RoundMode.SR draws for the accumulate rounding. Default: 0

  • accumulate_algorithm (AccumulateAlgorithm) – as for binaryK_matmul(). Default: AccumulateAlgorithm.NAIVE

  • rounding_mode (RoundMode) – the rounding of both formats. Default: RoundMode.RNE

  • saturation_mode (SaturationMode) – the multiply format’s overflow behavior. Default: SaturationMode.SAT_NONE

  • acc_saturation_mode (SaturationMode | None) – the accumulate format’s overflow behavior. Default: None, saturation_mode.

  • block_size (int | None) – as for binaryK_matmul(). Default: None

  • outer_man_bits (int | None) – mantissa bits of the outer format, the rounding BLOCK and TREE apply to the total after each block is folded in (binaryK_matmul()’s outer_K). The four widths are given together, or none of them, which leaves the total in the carrier’s precision. Default: None

  • outer_exp_bits (int | None) – exponent bits of the outer format. Default: None

  • outer_normal_binades (int | None) – normal binades of the outer format. Default: None

  • outer_bias (int | None) – exponent bias of the outer format. Default: None

  • outer_is_signed (bool | None) – whether the outer format has a sign bit. Default: None, the accumulate format’s.

  • outer_prng_bits (int) – random bits RoundMode.SR draws for the outer rounding. Default: 0

  • outer_saturation_mode (SaturationMode | None) – the outer format’s overflow behavior. Default: None, the accumulate format’s.

  • carrier (dtype | None) – as for binaryK_matmul(). Default: None, the operands’ own carrier.

  • carrier_rounding (RoundMode) – as for binaryK_matmul(). Default: RoundMode.RNE

Returns:

the product, in the operands’ dtype, with the shape torch.matmul would give.

Return type:

Tensor

Raises:

  • ValueError – if a carrier cannot hold a format (as for superfp_quantize()), if carrier names no carrier or is narrower than the operands, or if the operands’ leading dimensions do not broadcast.

  • TypeError – if carrier is neither a torch.dtype nor None.

  • RuntimeError – if the inner dimensions do not match, the operands differ in dtype or device, or an operand requires grad under grad mode.

Warns:

FormatRangeWarning – if a format’s range outruns the carrier’s, or the accumulate format’s range reaches past a narrower result dtype’s.

Example:

>>> a = torch.tensor([[1.0, 2.0], [3.0, 4.0]])
>>> superfp_matmul(
...     a, a, mul_man_bits=3, mul_exp_bits=4, mul_normal_binades=8, mul_bias=7
... )
tensor([[ 7., 10.],
        [15., 22.]])

Quantized GEMM with a fused multiply-add in a binaryK format.

The fused analog of binaryK_matmul(). Every dot-product step is a single hardware-style fused multiply-add: s + a * b, with s the running sum, rounded once. The multiply and the accumulate are not rounded separately. A real FMA unit has one output rounding, so there is a single fma_K/fma_P format instead of a mul_*/acc_* pair. With fma_quant=False the fused step runs at the carrier’s own precision, like accumulate_quant=False in binaryK_matmul().

a and b follow torch.matmul’s operand rules. The carrier, the storage check and the per-call resolution are as for binaryK_matmul().

Parameters:

  • a (Tensor) – the left operand; float32, float64, float16 or bfloat16.

  • b (Tensor) – the right operand, of a’s dtype and device.

  • trans_a (bool) – read a transposed in its last two dimensions. Default: False

  • trans_b (bool) – read b transposed in its last two dimensions. Default: False

  • fma_K (int) – width in bits of the fused step’s format.

  • fma_P (int) – precision of the fused step’s format.

  • fma_bias (int | None) – its exponent bias. Default: None, P3109’s 2**(K - P - 1) signed and 2**(K - P) unsigned.

  • fma_is_signed (bool) – whether the format has a sign bit. Default: True

  • fma_quant (bool) – whether the fused step is rounded to the format at all. Default: True

  • fma_prng_bits (int) – random bits RoundMode.SR draws for the fused rounding, as binaryK_quantize()’s prng_bits. Default: 0

  • accumulate_algorithm (AccumulateAlgorithm) – as for binaryK_matmul(), with the fused step in place of the split one, except TREE, which raises: a fused multiply-add has no product term to sum pairwise. Default: AccumulateAlgorithm.NAIVE

  • rounding_mode (RoundMode) – the fused step’s rounding. Default: RoundMode.RNE

  • saturation_mode (SaturationMode) – the format’s overflow behavior. Default: SaturationMode.SAT_NONE

  • subnormals_mode (SubnormalsMode) – the format’s bottom of range. Default: SubnormalsMode.SUBNORMALS

  • block_size (int | None) – as for binaryK_matmul(). Default: None

  • outer_K (int | None) – as for binaryK_matmul(). Default: None

  • outer_P (int | None) – as for binaryK_matmul(). Default: None

  • outer_bias (int | None) – as for binaryK_matmul(). Default: None

  • outer_is_signed (bool | None) – whether the outer format has a sign bit. Default: None, fma_is_signed.

  • outer_prng_bits (int) – as for binaryK_matmul(). Default: 0

  • outer_saturation_mode (SaturationMode | None) – the outer format’s overflow behavior. Default: None, saturation_mode.

  • outer_subnormals_mode (SubnormalsMode | None) – the outer format’s bottom of range. Default: None, subnormals_mode.

  • carrier (dtype | None) – as for binaryK_matmul(). Default: None, the operands’ own carrier.

  • carrier_rounding (RoundMode) – as for binaryK_matmul(). The fused step needs fma_quant=True. Default: RoundMode.RNE

Returns:

the product, in the operands’ dtype, with the shape torch.matmul would give.

Return type:

Tensor

Raises:

  • ValueError – if a carrier cannot hold the format, if carrier names no carrier or is narrower than the operands, or if the operands’ leading dimensions do not broadcast.

  • TypeError – if carrier is neither a torch.dtype nor None.

  • RuntimeError – if the inner dimensions do not match, the operands differ in dtype or device, or an operand requires grad under grad mode.

Warns:

FormatRangeWarning – if the format’s range outruns the carrier’s or reaches past a narrower result dtype’s.

Example:

>>> a = torch.tensor([[1.0, 2.0], [3.0, 4.0]])
>>> binaryK_matmul_fma(a, a, fma_K=8, fma_P=3)
tensor([[ 7., 10.],
        [16., 24.]])

Quantized GEMM whose binaryK format varies per output element.

The palette analog of binaryK_matmul(). The arithmetic is the same split one, a rounded multiply followed by a rounded accumulate. The difference is that the binaryK format of each output element’s dot product is chosen by prec_idx from a palette of up to 8 formats.

mul_K and mul_P are per-entry sequences, and their common length is the palette size n. Each of the other palette arguments may be a scalar (used for every entry), an n-length sequence, or None. None defaults per entry as in binaryK_matmul(): acc_* fall back to the mul_* entry, and a bias to P3109’s. Every entry is checked against the call’s carrier, and every accumulate entry against a narrower result dtype.

prec_idx selects a palette entry per output element. Its shape must be the GEMM’s output shape [M, N] (dense), [M, 1] (per row) or [1, N] (per column). It may have a leading batch dimension of B (one map per batch element) or 1. The batch is never folded into M here, because the map is indexed by output element.

Any integer dtype and layout is accepted. A map that is already int32, contiguous and on a’s device is passed through unchanged. Any other map is narrowed and packed on every call. On CUDA the bounds check reads the map’s extremes back to the host, so it is memoized on the map tensor’s identity and version. Keep one map and reuse it across calls; a map rebuilt per call is re-checked per call.

Parameters:

  • a (Tensor) – the left operand; float32, float64, float16 or bfloat16.

  • b (Tensor) – the right operand, of a’s dtype and device.

  • prec_idx (Tensor) – the palette index of each output element, in [0, n).

  • trans_a (bool) – read a transposed in its last two dimensions. Default: False

  • trans_b (bool) – read b transposed in its last two dimensions. Default: False

  • mul_K (Sequence[int]) – width in bits of each entry’s multiply format.

  • mul_P (Sequence[int]) – precision of each entry’s multiply format.

  • mul_bias (int | Sequence[int] | None) – exponent bias of each entry’s multiply format. Default: None, P3109’s per entry.

  • mul_is_signed (bool) – whether the multiply formats have a sign bit; shared by the palette. Default: True

  • mul_prng_bits (int) – random bits RoundMode.SR draws for the multiply rounding; shared by the palette. Default: 0

  • accumulate_quant (bool) – whether the running sum is rounded to the accumulate format after every step. Default: True

  • acc_K (int | Sequence[int] | None) – width of each entry’s accumulate format. Default: None, the mul_K entry.

  • acc_P (int | Sequence[int] | None) – precision of each entry’s accumulate format. Default: None, the mul_P entry.

  • acc_bias (int | Sequence[int] | None) – exponent bias of each entry’s accumulate format. Default: None, P3109’s per entry.

  • acc_is_signed (bool | None) – whether the accumulate formats have a sign bit. Default: None, mul_is_signed.

  • acc_prng_bits (int) – random bits RoundMode.SR draws for the accumulate rounding. Default: 0

  • accumulate_algorithm (AccumulateAlgorithm) – how the products are summed; the palette ops implement NAIVE only. Default: AccumulateAlgorithm.NAIVE

  • rounding_mode (RoundMode) – the rounding of every format. Default: RoundMode.RNE

  • saturation_mode (SaturationMode) – the multiply formats’ overflow behavior. Default: SaturationMode.SAT_NONE

  • subnormals_mode (SubnormalsMode) – the multiply formats’ bottom of range. Default: SubnormalsMode.SUBNORMALS

  • acc_saturation_mode (SaturationMode | None) – the accumulate formats’ overflow behavior. Default: None, saturation_mode.

  • acc_subnormals_mode (SubnormalsMode | None) – the accumulate formats’ bottom of range. Default: None, subnormals_mode.

  • carrier (dtype | None) – as for binaryK_matmul(). Default: None, the operands’ own carrier.

Returns:

the product, in the operands’ dtype, with the shape torch.matmul would give.

Return type:

Tensor

Raises:

  • ValueError – if the palette is empty or a palette argument’s length is not n, if a carrier cannot hold an entry, if carrier names no carrier or is narrower than the operands, or if the operands’ leading dimensions do not broadcast.

  • TypeError – if carrier is neither a torch.dtype nor None.

  • RuntimeError – if n is above 8, prec_idx has the wrong shape or an entry outside [0, n), the inner dimensions do not match, the operands differ in dtype or device, or an operand requires grad under grad mode.

Warns:

FormatRangeWarning – if an entry’s range outruns the carrier’s, or an accumulate entry’s range reaches past a narrower result dtype’s.

Example:

>>> a = torch.tensor([[1.0, 2.0], [3.0, 4.0]])
>>> prec_idx = torch.tensor([[0, 0], [0, 1]])
>>> binaryK_matmul_mixed(a, a, prec_idx, mul_K=[8, 8], mul_P=[4, 3])
tensor([[ 7., 10.],
        [15., 24.]])

Three output elements use the P=4 entry and are exact. The last uses the P=3 entry, whose two mantissa bits round the sum 22 to 24.

Warns:

FormatRangeWarning – if an entry’s range outruns the carrier’s, or an accumulate entry’s range reaches past a narrower result dtype’s.

Example:

>>> a = torch.tensor([[1.0, 2.0], [3.0, 4.0]])
>>> prec_idx = torch.tensor([[0, 0], [0, 1]])
>>> superfp_matmul_mixed(
...     a, a, prec_idx, mul_man_bits=[3, 2], mul_exp_bits=[4, 4],
...     mul_normal_binades=8, mul_bias=7,
... )
tensor([[ 7., 10.],
        [15., 24.]])
mptorch.quant.binaryK_matmul_fma_mixed(a, b, prec_idx, *, trans_a=False, trans_b=False, fma_K, fma_P, fma_bias=None, fma_is_signed=True, fma_quant=True, fma_prng_bits=0, accumulate_algorithm=AccumulateAlgorithm.NAIVE, rounding_mode=RoundMode.RNE, saturation_mode=SaturationMode.SAT_NONE, subnormals_mode=SubnormalsMode.SUBNORMALS, carrier=None)[source]#

Quantized fused-multiply-add GEMM whose binaryK format varies per element.

The palette analog of binaryK_matmul_fma(). Each dot-product step is a single fused multiply-add, rounded once. The binaryK format of that rounding is chosen per output element by prec_idx, from a palette of up to 8 formats. prec_idx follows the contract of binaryK_matmul_mixed().

fma_K and fma_P are per-entry sequences, and their common length is the palette size n. fma_bias may be a scalar, an n-length sequence, or None for P3109’s bias per entry.

fma_quant=False is rejected. An unrounded fused step has no format, so a palette would leave prec_idx nothing to choose. Use binaryK_matmul_fma() for the unquantized fused step.

Parameters:

  • a (Tensor) – the left operand; float32, float64, float16 or bfloat16.

  • b (Tensor) – the right operand, of a’s dtype and device.

  • prec_idx (Tensor) – the palette index of each output element, in [0, n).

  • trans_a (bool) – read a transposed in its last two dimensions. Default: False

  • trans_b (bool) – read b transposed in its last two dimensions. Default: False

  • fma_K (Sequence[int]) – width in bits of each entry’s format.

  • fma_P (Sequence[int]) – precision of each entry’s format.

  • fma_bias (int | Sequence[int] | None) – exponent bias of each entry’s format. Default: None, P3109’s per entry.

  • fma_is_signed (bool) – whether the formats have a sign bit; shared by the palette. Default: True

  • fma_quant (bool) – must be True. Default: True

  • fma_prng_bits (int) – random bits RoundMode.SR draws for the fused rounding; shared by the palette. Default: 0

  • accumulate_algorithm (AccumulateAlgorithm) – how the fused steps are summed; the palette ops implement NAIVE only. Default: AccumulateAlgorithm.NAIVE

  • rounding_mode (RoundMode) – the rounding of every entry. Default: RoundMode.RNE

  • saturation_mode (SaturationMode) – the formats’ overflow behavior. Default: SaturationMode.SAT_NONE

  • subnormals_mode (SubnormalsMode) – the formats’ bottom of range. Default: SubnormalsMode.SUBNORMALS

  • carrier (dtype | None) – as for binaryK_matmul(). Default: None, the operands’ own carrier.

Returns:

the product, in the operands’ dtype, with the shape torch.matmul would give.

Return type:

Tensor

Raises:

  • ValueError – if the palette is empty or a palette argument’s length is not n, if a carrier cannot hold an entry, if carrier names no carrier or is narrower than the operands, or if the operands’ leading dimensions do not broadcast.

  • TypeError – if carrier is neither a torch.dtype nor None.

  • RuntimeError – if fma_quant is false, n is above 8, prec_idx has the wrong shape or an entry outside [0, n), the inner dimensions do not match, the operands differ in dtype or device, or an operand requires grad under grad mode.

Warns:

FormatRangeWarning – if an entry’s range outruns the carrier’s or reaches past a narrower result dtype’s.

Example:

>>> a = torch.tensor([[1.0, 2.0], [3.0, 4.0]])
>>> prec_idx = torch.tensor([[0, 0], [0, 1]])
>>> binaryK_matmul_fma_mixed(a, a, prec_idx, fma_K=[8, 8], fma_P=[4, 3])
tensor([[ 7., 10.],
        [15., 24.]])

mptorch.quant.binaryK_superfp_matmul(a, b, *, trans_a=False, trans_b=False, mul_K, mul_P, mul_bias=None, mul_is_signed=True, mul_prng_bits=0, acc_man_bits, acc_exp_bits, acc_normal_binades, acc_bias, acc_is_signed=None, acc_prng_bits=0, accumulate_algorithm=AccumulateAlgorithm.NAIVE, rounding_mode=RoundMode.RNE, saturation_mode=SaturationMode.SAT_NONE, subnormals_mode=SubnormalsMode.SUBNORMALS, acc_saturation_mode=None, block_size=None, outer_man_bits=None, outer_exp_bits=None, outer_normal_binades=None, outer_bias=None, outer_is_signed=None, outer_prng_bits=0, outer_saturation_mode=None, carrier=None)[source]#

Quantized GEMM whose products are binaryK and whose sums are superfp.

The cross-family split multiply-accumulate: each step computes s = round_acc(s + round_mul(a * b)) in the carrier, as binaryK_matmul() does, with the product rounded to the binaryK format mul_K/mul_P and the partial sum to the superfp format given by the four acc_* widths. The accumulate format is required: a sum left in the carrier is binaryK_matmul() with accumulate_quant=False. binaryK_matmul() describes the general contract (torch.matmul’s operand rules, the transpose flags, the carrier, the storage check, the per-call resolution) and superfp_quantize() the accumulate format. The result holds the accumulate format’s values, or with BLOCK or TREE and an outer format, the outer format’s, which is of the accumulate’s family.

mptorch.quant.SplitMac with a mptorch.BinaryK multiply and a mptorch.SuperFP accumulate resolves to this op.

Parameters:

  • a (Tensor) – the left operand; float32, float64, float16 or bfloat16.

  • b (Tensor) – the right operand, of a’s dtype and device.

  • trans_a (bool) – read a transposed in its last two dimensions. Default: False

  • trans_b (bool) – read b transposed in its last two dimensions. Default: False

  • mul_K (int) – width in bits of the binaryK multiply format.

  • mul_P (int) – precision of the multiply format.

  • mul_bias (int | None) – exponent bias of the multiply format. Default: None, P3109’s 2**(K - P - 1) signed and 2**(K - P) unsigned.

  • mul_is_signed (bool) – whether the multiply format has a sign bit. Default: True

  • mul_prng_bits (int) – random bits RoundMode.SR draws for the multiply rounding. Default: 0

  • acc_man_bits (int) – stored mantissa bits of the superfp accumulate format.

  • acc_exp_bits (int) – exponent bits of the accumulate format.

  • acc_normal_binades (int) – binades of the accumulate format that carry the mantissa.

  • acc_bias (int) – exponent bias of the accumulate format.

  • acc_is_signed (bool | None) – whether the accumulate format has a sign bit. Default: None, mul_is_signed.

  • acc_prng_bits (int) – random bits RoundMode.SR draws for the accumulate rounding. Default: 0

  • accumulate_algorithm (AccumulateAlgorithm) – as for binaryK_matmul(). Default: AccumulateAlgorithm.NAIVE

  • rounding_mode (RoundMode) – the rounding of both formats. Default: RoundMode.RNE

  • saturation_mode (SaturationMode) – the multiply format’s overflow behavior. Default: SaturationMode.SAT_NONE

  • subnormals_mode (SubnormalsMode) – the multiply format’s bottom of range. Default: SubnormalsMode.SUBNORMALS

  • acc_saturation_mode (SaturationMode | None) – the accumulate format’s overflow behavior. Default: None, saturation_mode.

  • block_size (int | None) – as for binaryK_matmul(). Default: None

  • outer_man_bits (int | None) – mantissa bits of the superfp outer format, as superfp_matmul()’s. The four widths are given together, or none of them. Default: None

  • outer_exp_bits (int | None) – exponent bits of the outer format. Default: None

  • outer_normal_binades (int | None) – normal binades of the outer format. Default: None

  • outer_bias (int | None) – exponent bias of the outer format. Default: None

  • outer_is_signed (bool | None) – whether the outer format has a sign bit. Default: None, the accumulate format’s.

  • outer_prng_bits (int) – random bits RoundMode.SR draws for the outer rounding. Default: 0

  • outer_saturation_mode (SaturationMode | None) – the outer format’s overflow behavior. Default: None, the accumulate format’s.

  • carrier (dtype | None) – as for binaryK_quantize(). torch.float64 widens narrower operands to binary64 and narrows the result back to their dtype with one rounding. torch.float32 refuses float64 operands. Default: None, the operands’ own carrier.

Returns:

the product, in the operands’ dtype, with the shape torch.matmul would give.

Return type:

Tensor

Raises:

  • ValueError – if a carrier cannot hold a format, if carrier is torch.float64 or names no carrier, if the operands are float64, or if their leading dimensions do not broadcast.

  • TypeError – if carrier is neither a torch.dtype nor None.

  • RuntimeError – if the inner dimensions do not match, the operands differ in dtype or device, or an operand requires grad under grad mode.

Warns:

FormatRangeWarning – if a format’s range outruns the carrier’s, or the accumulate format’s range reaches past a narrower result dtype’s.

Example:

>>> a = torch.tensor([[1.0, 2.0], [3.0, 4.0]])
>>> binaryK_superfp_matmul(
...     a, a, mul_K=8, mul_P=4,
...     acc_man_bits=2, acc_exp_bits=4, acc_normal_binades=8, acc_bias=7,
... )
tensor([[ 7., 10.],
        [16., 24.]])

Every product is exact in Binary8p4. The sums 15 and 22 fall halfway between values of the superfp accumulate format, whose two mantissa bits space them 2 apart in [8, 16) and 4 apart in [16, 32), and round to the even mantissa: 16 and 24.

Quantized GEMM whose products are superfp and whose sums are binaryK.

binaryK_superfp_matmul() with the families exchanged: each product is rounded to the superfp format given by the four mul_* widths and each partial sum to the binaryK format acc_K/acc_P, which is required (a sum left in the carrier is superfp_matmul() with accumulate_quant=False). With BLOCK or TREE the outer format is a binaryK one, as binaryK_matmul()’s. mptorch.quant.SplitMac with a mptorch.SuperFP multiply and a mptorch.BinaryK accumulate resolves to this op.

class mptorch.quant.QAffineFormats(weight_quant=None, input_quant=None, bias_quant=None, wgrad_quant=None, igrad_quant=None, bgrad_quant=None, fwd_math=None, bwd_igrad_math=None, bwd_wgrad_math=None, recompute_input=None, recompute_weight=None)[source]#

Quantizers and custom math for an affine layer (Linear, Conv1d/2d/3d).

Every slot is optional, and None means plain PyTorch behaviour for that step. Quantization is therefore opt-in per tensor and per pass: with a QAffineFormats() that has nothing set, QLinear behaves exactly as nn.Linear.

The forward pass quantizes the input, the weight and the bias through their *_quant slots, then runs fwd_math (or the plain op). The backward pass quantizes the incoming gradient separately for the input-gradient path (igrad_quant) and the weight-gradient path (wgrad_quant), because the two GEMMs may need different formats. It then runs bwd_igrad_math and bwd_wgrad_math (or PyTorch’s defaults).

The class inherits from nn.Module. A quantizer that is itself an nn.Module (a QAT observer with running statistics) is therefore registered with the parent model and appears in its state_dict.

Backward needs the quantized input (for the weight gradient) and the quantized weight (for the input gradient) again. The layer can keep each as a quantized copy, a tensor the size of the operand, or keep the raw operand and quantize it again in backward, which saves the copy wherever the raw operand is alive anyway: the weight always is, and an input is when the op that made it keeps its output (ReLU does). The two recompute_* flags choose; None is the layer’s default (both for QConv1d/2d/3d, the weight only for QLinear). Gradients are bit-identical either way: under stochastic rounding the second call sees the random generators as the first did. Layers (“What a layer keeps for backward”) says when each choice saves memory.

Parameters:

  • weight_quant (Callable | None) – applied to the weight in the forward. Default: None

  • input_quant (Callable | None) – applied to the input in the forward. Default: None

  • bias_quant (Callable | None) – applied to the bias in the forward. Default: None

  • wgrad_quant (Callable | None) – applied to the output gradient before the weight-gradient GEMM. Default: None

  • igrad_quant (Callable | None) – applied to the output gradient before the input-gradient GEMM. Default: None

  • bgrad_quant (Callable | None) – applied to the output gradient before the bias-gradient sum. Default: None

  • fwd_math (Callable | None) – the forward’s arithmetic. For Linear, fwd_math(q_input, q_weight, q_bias); for Conv, the same plus stride, padding, dilation, groups and nd as keywords. Default: None

  • bwd_igrad_math (Callable | None) – the input gradient’s arithmetic, bwd_igrad_math(q_grad_output, q_weight) for Linear (Conv adds input_size and the convolution keywords). Default: None

  • bwd_wgrad_math (Callable | None) – the weight gradient’s arithmetic, bwd_wgrad_math(q_grad_output, q_input) for Linear (Conv adds weight_size and the convolution keywords). Default: None

  • recompute_input (bool | None) – keep the raw input for backward and run input_quant on it again there, instead of keeping its result. None is the layer’s default: True for a convolution, False for QLinear. Under None only a quantizer known to be stateless is run twice – a mptorch.quant.Quant (not in place), a mptorch.quant.BlockQuant called as a fake quantizer, or a mptorch.quant.Quantizer over one – and any other callable keeps its result saved, since one with state (a QAT observer) would update it twice. True runs any callable again, which is the caller’s promise that it depends only on its input and the random generators. A quantizer whose result is not a tensor (a packed block format) keeps it saved. Default: None

  • recompute_weight (bool | None) – the same for the weight and weight_quant. None is True for every layer, since the raw weight is alive anyway as the layer’s parameter. Default: None

Example:

>>> from mptorch import BinaryK
>>> from mptorch.quant import QAffineFormats, QLinear, Quant, binaryK_gemm_formats
>>> formats = binaryK_gemm_formats(mul_K=8, mul_P=4, accumulate_quant=False)
>>> formats.input_quant = Quant(BinaryK(8, 4))
>>> formats.weight_quant = Quant(BinaryK(8, 4))
>>> layer = QLinear(256, 64, formats=formats)
>>> plain = QLinear(256, 64, formats=QAffineFormats())   # as nn.Linear

Initialize internal Module state, shared by both nn.Module and ScriptModule.

class mptorch.quant.QLinear(in_features, out_features, bias=True, device=None, dtype=None, formats=None)[source]#

torch.nn.Linear with per-tensor quantization and custom arithmetic.

It holds the same parameters as nn.Linear and computes the same input @ weight.T + bias, but through CustomArithLinear. The input, the weight, the bias and each gradient can therefore be rounded by the quantizers in formats, and each GEMM can run in custom arithmetic (see mptorch.quant.binaryK_gemm_formats()). With formats left None, or with a QAffineFormats whose slots are all None, the layer is numerically identical to nn.Linear. formats is a submodule, so a stateful quantizer in it appears in the layer’s state_dict. For backward the layer keeps a quantized copy of its input and its raw weight, which it quantizes again there, unless formats’ recompute_input / recompute_weight say otherwise. A layer over mptorch.quant.block_gemm_formats() can drop its float weight for its block codes with freeze_packed_().

Parameters:

  • in_features (int) – size of each input sample.

  • out_features (int) – size of each output sample.

  • bias (bool) – whether the layer learns an additive bias. Default: True

  • device – as for nn.Linear. Default: None

  • dtype – as for nn.Linear. Default: None

  • formats (QAffineFormats | None) – the quantizers and math hooks. None builds an empty QAffineFormats(). Default: None

Shape:

  • Input: (*, in_features), any number of leading dimensions.

  • Output: (*, out_features).

Example:

>>> import torch
>>> from mptorch import BinaryK
>>> from mptorch.quant import QLinear, Quant, binaryK_gemm_formats
>>> formats = binaryK_gemm_formats(mul_K=8, mul_P=4, acc_K=16, acc_P=11)
>>> formats.input_quant = Quant(BinaryK(8, 4))
>>> formats.weight_quant = Quant(BinaryK(8, 4))
>>> layer = QLinear(256, 64, formats=formats)
>>> layer(torch.randn(32, 256)).shape
torch.Size([32, 64])

forward(input)[source]#

Runs the forward pass.

Return type:

Tensor

Parameters:

input (Tensor)

freeze_packed_(*, pack=True)[source]#

Replace the float weight by its block codes, in place.

The layer becomes a QPackedLinear: its weight is None, and two uint8 buffers, weight_codes and weight_scales, hold the weight packed along its input features. The codes are what the layer’s forward multiplies, so the frozen layer returns what it returned before:

  • with formats.weight_quant unset, the weight packed in the weight format of mptorch.quant.block_gemm_formats();

  • with weight_quant = BlockQuant(fmt, axis=1).pack, that packing: the memoized one, if the weight has not changed since the last forward (its stochastic draws included), and the memo is then cleared, since it would keep the codes alive;

  • with another quantizer, the weight format’s packing of its result.

Nothing is kept of the float weight, so its memory is freed once nothing else refers to it: freeze before building an optimizer or any copy of the parameters. A square-tiled weight still serves the input gradient, so layers below a frozen one can train; there is no weight gradient, and the bias stays a float parameter.

Parameters:

pack (bool) – pack the weight. False allocates zeroed buffers of the right shapes instead, on the weight’s device, for load_state_dict() of a frozen checkpoint to fill; on the meta device it allocates nothing. Default: True

Returns:

this layer.

Return type:

QPackedLinear

Raises:

  • ValueError – for formats that do not come from mptorch.quant.block_gemm_formats(), for pack=True on a weight on the meta device, which has no values, and for a weight_quant result the block hooks cannot multiply.

  • TypeError – for a layer that is frozen already (quantizing twice is not always the identity), or of a subclass of QLinear, whose class the switch would drop.

Example:

>>> import torch
>>> from mptorch import BinaryK, MXFP8_E4M3
>>> from mptorch.quant import QLinear, block_gemm_formats
>>> layer = QLinear(64, 32, formats=block_gemm_formats(MXFP8_E4M3, MXFP8_E4M3))
>>> x = torch.randn(4, 64)
>>> with torch.no_grad():
...     before = layer(x)
...     _ = layer.freeze_packed_()
...     torch.equal(layer(x), before), layer.weight
(True, None)
>>> sorted(layer.state_dict())
['_extra_state', 'bias', 'weight_codes', 'weight_scales']
class mptorch.quant.QPackedLinear(*args, **kwargs)[source]#

A QLinear whose weight is stored only as its block codes.

QLinear.freeze_packed_() and mptorch.quant.freeze_packed_() make one, in place, from a QLinear over mptorch.quant.block_gemm_formats(); the class is not constructed directly. It is still a QLinear (isinstance holds) and returns what the layer returned before the freeze, from a fraction of the memory: the weight’s codes and scales are uint8 buffers, weight_codes and weight_scales, which follow .to() and stay uint8 under .half(), and weight is None. The packing’s format, shape, tensor scale, dtype and carrier are in the state_dict’s _extra_state, as plain values.

The format itself is code, as every hook of the layer’s formats is. To load a frozen checkpoint, build the model as it was built, freeze it with pack=False, which allocates zeroed codes and packs nothing, and load the state_dict. A model built on the meta device and frozen that way allocates its codes only when the state is loaded with assign=True, so the float model never exists. A checkpoint frozen in another format or shape raises, naming both.

packed_weight is the codes as a mptorch.quant.BlockPacked, and unfreeze_packed_() turns the layer back into a QLinear.

  • kwargs (Any)

unfreeze_packed_()[source]#

Turn the layer back into a QLinear, in place, whose float weight is the decoded codes (mptorch.quant.block_unpack()): the quantized weight, not the one the layer was frozen from, in the dtype it was packed from. For fine-tuning from a frozen checkpoint, or exporting to tools that read a plain nn.Linear.

Return type:

QLinear

mptorch.quant.freeze_packed_(model, *, pack=True)[source]#

QLinear.freeze_packed_() on every QLinear of model whose formats come from mptorch.quant.block_gemm_formats().

The layers are frozen one at a time, so the freeze holds at most one layer’s float weight and its codes at once beyond the model. A model that does not fit on its device as float can be frozen on the CPU and then moved. Other modules are left as they are.

Parameters:

  • model (Module) – the model, or one layer.

  • pack (bool) – as for QLinear.freeze_packed_(): False allocates zeroed codes for a frozen checkpoint to fill. Default: True

Returns:

how many layers were frozen.

Return type:

int

Example:

>>> import torch
>>> from torch import nn
>>> from mptorch import BinaryK, MXFP8_E4M3
>>> from mptorch.quant import QLinear, block_gemm_formats, freeze_packed_
>>> def mlp():
...     return nn.Sequential(
...         QLinear(64, 64, formats=block_gemm_formats(MXFP8_E4M3, MXFP8_E4M3)),
...         nn.ReLU(),
...         QLinear(64, 8, formats=block_gemm_formats(MXFP8_E4M3, MXFP8_E4M3)),
...     )
>>> model = mlp()
>>> freeze_packed_(model)
2
>>> skeleton = mlp()  # load: build, freeze without packing, then load
>>> freeze_packed_(skeleton, pack=False)
2
>>> skeleton.load_state_dict(model.state_dict())
<All keys matched successfully>
class mptorch.quant.QConv1d(in_channels, out_channels, kernel_size, stride=1, padding=0, dilation=1, groups=1, bias=True, padding_mode='zeros', device=None, dtype=None, formats=None)[source]#

torch.nn.Conv1d with per-tensor quantization and custom arithmetic.

It holds the same parameters as nn.Conv1d and computes the same convolution, but through CustomArithConvNd. The input, the weight, the bias and each gradient can therefore be rounded by the quantizers in formats, and each convolution can run in custom arithmetic. With formats left None, or with a QAffineFormats whose slots are all None, the layer is numerically identical to nn.Conv1d. A padding_mode other than "zeros" is applied with F.pad before the Function, as nn.Conv1d does, so the Function only ever sees zero padding. For backward the layer keeps its raw input and weight, which it quantizes again there, unless formats’ recompute_input / recompute_weight say otherwise.

Parameters:

  • in_channels (int) – channels of the input.

  • out_channels (int) – channels of the output.

  • kernel_size (int | tuple[int]) – size of the convolving kernel.

  • stride (int | tuple[int]) – stride of the convolution. Default: 1

  • padding (int | tuple[int] | str) – padding added to both sides of the input. Default: 0

  • dilation (int | tuple[int]) – spacing between kernel elements. Default: 1

  • groups (int) – blocked connections from input to output channels. Default: 1

  • bias (bool) – whether the layer learns an additive bias. Default: True

  • padding_mode (Literal['zeros', 'reflect', 'replicate', 'circular']) – "zeros", "reflect", "replicate" or "circular". Default: "zeros"

  • device – as for nn.Conv1d. Default: None

  • dtype – as for nn.Conv1d. Default: None

  • formats (QAffineFormats | None) – the quantizers and math hooks; mptorch.quant.conv_formats() builds hooks that run the three convolutions in a custom arithmetic. None builds an empty QAffineFormats(). Default: None

Shape:

  • Input: (N, C_in, L_in) or (C_in, L_in).

  • Output: (N, C_out, L_out) or (C_out, L_out), as for nn.Conv1d.

Example:

>>> import torch
>>> from mptorch import BinaryK
>>> from mptorch.quant import QAffineFormats, QConv1d, Quant
>>> formats = QAffineFormats(weight_quant=Quant(BinaryK(8, 4)))
>>> conv = QConv1d(3, 8, 3, formats=formats)
>>> conv(torch.randn(1, 3, 16)).shape
torch.Size([1, 8, 14])

torch.nn.Conv2d with per-tensor quantization and custom arithmetic.

The 2D twin of QConv1d. It has the same parameters as nn.Conv2d and computes the same convolution, through CustomArithConvNd, so the quantizers and math hooks in formats apply. With empty formats it is numerically identical to nn.Conv2d.

Shape:

The 3D twin of QConv1d. It has the same parameters as nn.Conv3d and computes the same convolution, through CustomArithConvNd, so the quantizers and math hooks in formats apply. With empty formats it is numerically identical to nn.Conv3d.

Layer arithmetic factories#

mptorch.quant.binaryK_gemm_formats(mul_K, mul_P, *, mul_bias=None, mul_is_signed=True, mul_prng_bits=0, accumulate_quant=True, acc_K=None, acc_P=None, acc_bias=None, acc_is_signed=None, acc_prng_bits=0, accumulate_algorithm=AccumulateAlgorithm.NAIVE, rounding_mode=RoundMode.RNE, saturation_mode=SaturationMode.SAT_NONE, subnormals_mode=SubnormalsMode.SUBNORMALS, acc_saturation_mode=None, acc_subnormals_mode=None, block_size=None, outer_K=None, outer_P=None, outer_bias=None, outer_is_signed=None, outer_prng_bits=0, outer_saturation_mode=None, outer_subnormals_mode=None, carrier=None, carrier_rounding=RoundMode.RNE)[source]#

Build a QAffineFormats whose dot products run in a binaryK GEMM.

The returned formats set fwd_math, bwd_igrad_math and bwd_wgrad_math. A Linear layer’s forward GEMM and both of its gradient GEMMs then run through mptorch.quant.ops.binaryK_matmul(), which takes these same arguments. Every product is rounded to the mul_* format. When accumulate_quant is set, every partial sum is rounded to the acc_* format.

The format is resolved once, here, so each pass costs only the op. Every pass checks the formats against the carrier of the tensors it runs on: binary64 for a float64 layer and binary32 otherwise, unless carrier names one. It warns with mptorch.FormatRangeWarning about a range that the carrier cannot hold.

Parameters:

  • mul_K (int) – total width in bits of the multiply format.

  • mul_P (int) – precision (significand bits, the implicit one included) of the multiply format.

  • mul_bias (int | None) – exponent bias of the multiply format. None takes IEEE P3109’s, 2**(K-P-1) signed and 2**(K-P) unsigned. Default: None

  • mul_is_signed (bool) – whether the multiply format has a sign bit. Default: True

  • mul_prng_bits (int) – random bits drawn per stochastic rounding of a product; only read when rounding_mode is RoundMode.SR. Default: 0

  • accumulate_quant (bool) – whether the running sum is rounded to the acc_* format after every step. False keeps it in the carrier’s precision and ignores the acc_* widths. Default: True

  • acc_K (int | None) – width of the accumulate format. None takes mul_K. Default: None

  • acc_P (int | None) – precision of the accumulate format. None takes mul_P. Default: None

  • acc_bias (int | None) – exponent bias of the accumulate format. None takes P3109’s for acc_K/acc_P. Default: None

  • acc_is_signed (bool | None) – sign bit of the accumulate format. None takes mul_is_signed. Default: None

  • acc_prng_bits (int) – random bits per stochastic rounding of a partial sum. Default: 0

  • accumulate_algorithm (AccumulateAlgorithm) – how the products are summed, as for mptorch.quant.binaryK_matmul(): NAIVE, KAHAN, BLOCK or TREE (the last not for a fused mac). Default: AccumulateAlgorithm.NAIVE

  • rounding_mode (RoundMode) – rounding for both formats; one mode for both because the kernels take it as a template parameter. Default: RoundMode.RNE

  • saturation_mode (SaturationMode) – overflow behaviour of the multiply format. Default: SaturationMode.SAT_NONE

  • subnormals_mode (SubnormalsMode) – what the multiply format keeps below its smallest normal. Default: SubnormalsMode.SUBNORMALS

  • acc_saturation_mode (SaturationMode | None) – overflow behaviour of the accumulate format. None takes saturation_mode. Default: None

  • acc_subnormals_mode (SubnormalsMode | None) – subnormal handling of the accumulate format. None takes subnormals_mode. Default: None

  • block_size (int | None) – BLOCK’s and TREE’s block size, as for mptorch.quant.binaryK_matmul(). Default: None

  • outer_K (int | None) – width of the outer format BLOCK and TREE round their total to, as for mptorch.quant.binaryK_matmul(), which documents it and the rest of its spelling: outer_P, outer_bias, outer_is_signed, outer_prng_bits, outer_saturation_mode and outer_subnormals_mode. Default: None, an unrounded total.

  • carrier (dtype | None) – the float arithmetic the GEMM rounds in. None takes the layer’s (binary64 for float64, binary32 for the rest); torch.float64 runs a float32 or half-precision layer in binary64 too and narrows each result back to the layer’s dtype; torch.float32 on a float64 layer raises at the call. Default: None

  • carrier_rounding (RoundMode) – RoundMode.RO rounds the carrier’s steps to odd, as for mptorch.quant.binaryK_matmul(), for every pass of the layer; NAIVE only. Default: RoundMode.RNE

  • outer_P (int | None)

  • outer_bias (int | None)

  • outer_is_signed (bool | None)

  • outer_prng_bits (int)

  • outer_saturation_mode (SaturationMode | None)

  • outer_subnormals_mode (SubnormalsMode | None)

Returns:

with the three *_math hooks set and every *_quant slot left None.

Return type:

QAffineFormats

Raises:

ValueError – for a format no carrier can hold (precision above 53 bits, an exponent field past 30 bits, stochastic bits with no significand left) or a carrier that names no carrier.

Example:

>>> import torch
>>> from mptorch import BinaryK
>>> from mptorch.quant import QLinear, Quant, binaryK_gemm_formats
>>> formats = binaryK_gemm_formats(mul_K=8, mul_P=4, acc_K=16, acc_P=11)
>>> formats.input_quant = Quant(BinaryK(8, 4))
>>> layer = QLinear(256, 64, formats=formats)
>>> layer(torch.randn(32, 256)).shape
torch.Size([32, 64])
mptorch.quant.binaryK_gemm_formats_fma(fma_K, fma_P, *, fma_bias=None, fma_is_signed=True, fma_quant=True, fma_prng_bits=0, accumulate_algorithm=AccumulateAlgorithm.NAIVE, rounding_mode=RoundMode.RNE, saturation_mode=SaturationMode.SAT_NONE, subnormals_mode=SubnormalsMode.SUBNORMALS, block_size=None, outer_K=None, outer_P=None, outer_bias=None, outer_is_signed=None, outer_prng_bits=0, outer_saturation_mode=None, outer_subnormals_mode=None, carrier=None, carrier_rounding=RoundMode.RNE)[source]#

Fused-multiply-add analog of binaryK_gemm_formats().

Each dot-product step is one fused multiply-add, round_fma(s + a * b), rounded once to the fma_* format (mptorch.quant.ops.binaryK_matmul_fma()). It replaces a rounded multiply followed by a separately rounded add. The general contract is that of binaryK_gemm_formats(): resolution at construction, the carrier and the warnings.

Parameters:

  • fma_K (int) – total width in bits of the fused format.

  • fma_P (int) – precision of the fused format, the implicit bit included.

  • fma_bias (int | None) – exponent bias; None takes IEEE P3109’s. Default: None

  • fma_is_signed (bool) – whether the format has a sign bit. Default: True

  • fma_quant (bool) – whether each fused step is rounded at all. False runs unrounded fused steps in the carrier. Default: True

  • fma_prng_bits (int) – random bits per stochastic rounding; only read when rounding_mode is RoundMode.SR. Default: 0

  • accumulate_algorithm (AccumulateAlgorithm) – how the products are summed, as for mptorch.quant.binaryK_matmul(): NAIVE, KAHAN, BLOCK or TREE (the last not for a fused mac). Default: AccumulateAlgorithm.NAIVE

  • rounding_mode (RoundMode) – rounding of each fused step. Default: RoundMode.RNE

  • saturation_mode (SaturationMode) – overflow behaviour. Default: SaturationMode.SAT_NONE

  • subnormals_mode (SubnormalsMode) – subnormal handling. Default: SubnormalsMode.SUBNORMALS

  • block_size (int | None) – BLOCK’s and TREE’s block size, as for mptorch.quant.binaryK_matmul(). Default: None

  • outer_K (int | None) – width of the outer format BLOCK and TREE round their total to, as for mptorch.quant.binaryK_matmul(), which documents it and the rest of its spelling: outer_P, outer_bias, outer_is_signed, outer_prng_bits, outer_saturation_mode and outer_subnormals_mode. Default: None, an unrounded total.

  • carrier (dtype | None) – as for binaryK_gemm_formats(). Default: None

  • carrier_rounding (RoundMode) – RoundMode.RO rounds the carrier’s steps to odd, as for mptorch.quant.binaryK_matmul_fma(), for every pass of the layer; NAIVE only. Default: RoundMode.RNE

  • outer_P (int | None)

  • outer_bias (int | None)

  • outer_is_signed (bool | None)

  • outer_prng_bits (int)

  • outer_saturation_mode (SaturationMode | None)

  • outer_subnormals_mode (SubnormalsMode | None)

Returns:

with the three *_math hooks set.

Return type:

QAffineFormats

Raises:

ValueError – as for binaryK_gemm_formats().

Example:

>>> import torch
>>> from mptorch.quant import QLinear, binaryK_gemm_formats_fma
>>> layer = QLinear(256, 64, formats=binaryK_gemm_formats_fma(8, 4))
>>> layer(torch.randn(32, 256)).shape

mptorch.quant.superfp_gemm_formats(mul_man_bits, mul_exp_bits, mul_normal_binades, mul_bias, *, mul_is_signed=True, mul_prng_bits=0, accumulate_quant=True, acc_man_bits=None, acc_exp_bits=None, acc_normal_binades=None, acc_bias=None, acc_is_signed=None, acc_prng_bits=0, accumulate_algorithm=AccumulateAlgorithm.NAIVE, rounding_mode=RoundMode.RNE, saturation_mode=SaturationMode.SAT_NONE, acc_saturation_mode=None, block_size=None, outer_man_bits=None, outer_exp_bits=None, outer_normal_binades=None, outer_bias=None, outer_is_signed=None, outer_prng_bits=0, outer_saturation_mode=None, carrier=None, carrier_rounding=RoundMode.RNE)[source]#

superfp analog of binaryK_gemm_formats().

The dot products run through mptorch.quant.ops.superfp_matmul(). Products are rounded to the mul_* superfp format. When accumulate_quant is set, partial sums are rounded to the acc_* one. A superfp format keeps a mantissa in the top normal_binades binades of its range and spends the rest of its codes on supernormal values, which are powers of two with no mantissa. It has no subnormals, so there is no subnormals_mode. superfp_gemm_formats_fma() is the fused-multiply-add analog.

Parameters:

  • mul_man_bits (int) – mantissa bits of the multiply format.

  • mul_exp_bits (int) – exponent bits of the multiply format.

  • mul_normal_binades (int) – binades with a full mantissa in the multiply format.

  • mul_bias (int) – exponent bias of the multiply format (required; superfp has no conventional default).

  • mul_is_signed (bool) – whether the multiply format has a sign bit. Default: True

  • mul_prng_bits (int) – random bits per stochastic rounding of a product. Default: 0

  • accumulate_quant (bool) – whether partial sums are rounded to the acc_* format. Default: True

  • acc_man_bits (int | None) – None takes mul_man_bits. Default: None

  • acc_exp_bits (int | None) – None takes mul_exp_bits. Default: None

  • acc_normal_binades (int | None) – None takes mul_normal_binades. Default: None

  • acc_bias (int | None) – None takes mul_bias. Default: None

  • acc_is_signed (bool | None) – None takes mul_is_signed. Default: None

  • acc_prng_bits (int) – random bits per stochastic rounding of a partial sum. Default: 0

  • accumulate_algorithm (AccumulateAlgorithm) – how the products are summed, as for mptorch.quant.binaryK_matmul(): NAIVE, KAHAN, BLOCK or TREE (the last not for a fused mac). Default: AccumulateAlgorithm.NAIVE

  • rounding_mode (RoundMode) – rounding for both formats. Default: RoundMode.RNE

  • saturation_mode (SaturationMode) – overflow behaviour of the multiply format. Default: SaturationMode.SAT_NONE

  • acc_saturation_mode (SaturationMode | None) – None takes saturation_mode. Default: None

  • block_size (int | None) – BLOCK’s and TREE’s block size, as for mptorch.quant.binaryK_matmul(). Default: None

  • outer_man_bits (int | None) – mantissa bits of the outer format BLOCK and TREE round their total to, as for mptorch.quant.superfp_matmul(), which documents it and the rest of its spelling: outer_exp_bits, outer_normal_binades, outer_bias, outer_is_signed, outer_prng_bits and outer_saturation_mode. Default: None, an unrounded total.

  • carrier (dtype | None) – as for binaryK_gemm_formats(). Default: None

  • carrier_rounding (RoundMode) – RoundMode.RO rounds the carrier’s steps to odd, as for mptorch.quant.superfp_matmul(), for every pass of the layer; NAIVE only. Default: RoundMode.RNE

  • outer_exp_bits (int | None)

  • outer_normal_binades (int | None)

  • outer_bias (int | None)

  • outer_is_signed (bool | None)

Returns:

with the three *_math hooks set.
