QAffineFormats

Raises:

ValueError – for a format no carrier can hold, a normal_binades that leaves no supernormal codes, or a carrier that names no carrier.

Example:

>>> import torch
>>> from mptorch.quant import QLinear, superfp_gemm_formats
>>> formats = superfp_gemm_formats(3, 4, 8, 7, accumulate_quant=False)
>>> layer = QLinear(256, 64, formats=formats)
>>> layer(torch.randn(32, 256)).shape
torch.Size([32, 64])
mptorch.quant.superfp_gemm_formats_fma(fma_man_bits, fma_exp_bits, fma_normal_binades, fma_bias, *, fma_is_signed=True, fma_quant=True, fma_prng_bits=0, accumulate_algorithm=AccumulateAlgorithm.NAIVE, rounding_mode=RoundMode.RNE, saturation_mode=SaturationMode.SAT_NONE, block_size=None, outer_man_bits=None, outer_exp_bits=None, outer_normal_binades=None, outer_bias=None, outer_is_signed=None, outer_prng_bits=0, outer_saturation_mode=None, carrier=None, carrier_rounding=RoundMode.RNE)[source]#

superfp analog of binaryK_gemm_formats_fma().

Each dot-product step is one fused multiply-add, rounded once to the fma_* superfp format (mptorch.quant.ops.superfp_matmul_fma()). The arguments are the multiply-format arguments of superfp_gemm_formats() under the fma_ prefix, plus fma_quant, as in binaryK_gemm_formats_fma().

Parameters:

  • fma_man_bits (int) – mantissa bits of the fused format.

  • fma_exp_bits (int) – exponent bits of the fused format.

  • fma_normal_binades (int) – binades with a full mantissa.

  • fma_bias (int) – exponent bias (required).

  • fma_is_signed (bool) – whether the format has a sign bit. Default: True

  • fma_quant (bool) – whether each fused step is rounded at all. Default: True

  • fma_prng_bits (int) – random bits per stochastic rounding. Default: 0

  • accumulate_algorithm (AccumulateAlgorithm) – how the products are summed, as for mptorch.quant.binaryK_matmul(): NAIVE, KAHAN, BLOCK or TREE (the last not for a fused mac). Default: AccumulateAlgorithm.NAIVE

  • rounding_mode (RoundMode) – rounding of each fused step. Default: RoundMode.RNE

  • saturation_mode (SaturationMode) – overflow behaviour. Default: SaturationMode.SAT_NONE

  • block_size (int | None) – BLOCK’s and TREE’s block size, as for mptorch.quant.binaryK_matmul(). Default: None

  • outer_man_bits (int | None) – mantissa bits of the outer format BLOCK and TREE round their total to, as for mptorch.quant.superfp_matmul(), which documents it and the rest of its spelling: outer_exp_bits, outer_normal_binades, outer_bias, outer_is_signed, outer_prng_bits and outer_saturation_mode. Default: None, an unrounded total.

  • carrier (dtype | None) – as for binaryK_gemm_formats(). Default: None

  • carrier_rounding (RoundMode) – RoundMode.RO rounds the carrier’s steps to odd, as for mptorch.quant.superfp_matmul_fma(), for every pass of the layer; NAIVE only. Default: RoundMode.RNE

  • outer_exp_bits (int | None)

  • outer_normal_binades (int | None)

  • outer_bias (int | None)

  • outer_is_signed (bool | None)

  • outer_prng_bits (int)

  • outer_saturation_mode (SaturationMode | None)

Returns:

with the three *_math hooks set.

Return type:

QAffineFormats

Raises:

ValueError – as for superfp_gemm_formats().

Example:

>>> import torch
>>> from mptorch.quant import QLinear, superfp_gemm_formats_fma
>>> formats = superfp_gemm_formats_fma(3, 4, 8, 7)
>>> layer = QLinear(256, 64, formats=formats)
>>> layer(torch.randn(32, 256)).shape
torch.Size([32, 64])

mptorch.quant.conv_formats(mac, *, prec_idx=None, igrad_prec_idx=None, wgrad_prec_idx=None)[source]#

Build a QAffineFormats whose three convolution passes run in mac’s arithmetic.

The forward convolution, the input gradient and the weight gradient of a QConv1d, QConv2d or QConv3d each run in mac’s arithmetic. Every product and every addition of every dot product is rounded as a GEMM of that mac rounds it. The operands are gathered from the convolution’s tensors inside the kernel instead of being unfolded, so no pass allocates more than its result.

The forward pass and the weight gradient are each one GEMM, bit-identical to the GEMM of the same mac over F.unfold’s operands.

The input gradient is one GEMM per residue class of the stride, each over the kernel taps that reach its positions. A strided convolution’s gradient therefore costs what its forward pass does. A transposed convolution would cost stride**nd times more, because it sums the zeros it inserts. Under a NAIVE sum and a deterministic rounding the two are bit-identical, because adding a zero changes nothing there. Convolutions has the equations and says what differs in the other cases.

Any stride, padding ("same" and "valid" included), dilation and groups works. Groups share one launch. A depthwise convolution (one channel per group) uses a sixteenth of the kernel’s tile width, which is correct but not fast.

Like matmul_formats(), this sets only the math hooks. The caller adds operand quantization (weight_quant, input_quant and the other *_quant slots) separately.

The carrier is the GEMM’s: a float64 model rounds in binary64, and float32, float16 and bfloat16 ones in binary32, unless the mac names carrier=torch.float64. Then narrower operands are widened, each pass runs the binary64 kernels, and its result is narrowed back to their dtype, bit-identical to the pass on the widened operands. On MPS, which has no float64, binary32 is the only carrier.

Parameters:

  • mac (SplitMac | FusedMac | Number) – the dot-product arithmetic, resolved once through mptorch.quant.mac.spec_for_mac(). A bare Number means SplitMac(fmt, fmt). Every accumulate_algorithm applies, and a SplitMac may round its products and its sums in formats of two families, as for a GEMM. A palette selects the per-output-element ops, which need one map per pass.

  • prec_idx (Tensor | None) – the forward’s palette map, indexed like the output with its spatial dimensions flattened: [Cout, OUT] with OUT the number of output positions, [Cout, 1] (one format per output channel) or [1, OUT], optionally with a leading batch dimension. Required by, and only by, a palette mac. Default: None

  • igrad_prec_idx (Tensor | None) – the input gradient’s map, shaped the same way over [Cin, IN], with IN the number of input positions. The classes of a strided gradient read it at their own positions. Default: None

  • wgrad_prec_idx (Tensor | None) – the weight gradient’s map, over the weight as [Cout, Cin/groups * prod(kernel)], or [Cout, 1]. Default: None

Returns:

with fwd_math, bwd_igrad_math and bwd_wgrad_math set and every *_quant slot left None.

Return type:

QAffineFormats

Raises:

ValueError – for a palette mac without prec_idx, or a map given to a mac without a palette.

Example

Binary8p4 products summed in a 12-bit accumulator, with the operands also rounded to Binary8p4, for a strided layer. The backward pass runs both gradients in the same arithmetic:

>>> import torch
>>> from mptorch import AccumulateAlgorithm, BinaryK, RoundMode
>>> from mptorch.quant import FusedMac, QConv1d, QConv2d, Quant, SplitMac
>>> from mptorch.quant import conv_formats
>>> binary8p4 = BinaryK(8, 4)
>>> formats = conv_formats(SplitMac(binary8p4, BinaryK(12, 7)))
>>> formats.input_quant = formats.weight_quant = Quant(binary8p4)
>>> conv = QConv2d(3, 8, 3, stride=2, padding=1, formats=formats)
>>> x = torch.randn(2, 3, 16, 16, requires_grad=True)
>>> conv(x).sum().backward()
>>> x.grad.shape, conv.weight.grad.shape
(torch.Size([2, 3, 16, 16]), torch.Size([8, 3, 3, 3]))

Any mac: a fused multiply-add with Kahan summation under stochastic rounding, on a grouped, dilated 1D convolution:

>>> fma = FusedMac(BinaryK(12, 7, prng_bits=8), rounding=RoundMode.SR,
...                accumulate_algorithm=AccumulateAlgorithm.KAHAN)
>>> conv1d = QConv1d(4, 8, 3, dilation=2, groups=2, formats=conv_formats(fma))
>>> conv1d(torch.randn(1, 4, 20)).shape
torch.Size([1, 8, 16])

A palette, here one format per output channel of the forward (a [Cout, 1] map), and one per pass for the two gradients:

>>> pal = SplitMac([binary8p4, BinaryK(8, 5)], BinaryK(12, 7))
>>> per_channel = conv_formats(
...     pal,
...     prec_idx=torch.tensor([[0], [1]] * 4),
...     igrad_prec_idx=torch.zeros(3, 1, dtype=torch.int64),
...     wgrad_prec_idx=torch.zeros(8, 1, dtype=torch.int64),
... )
>>> QConv2d(3, 8, 3, padding=1, formats=per_channel)(torch.randn(1, 3, 6, 6)).shape
torch.Size([1, 8, 6, 6])
mptorch.quant.block_gemm_formats(input, weight, grad=None, *, acc=None, fused=False, rounding=RoundMode.RNE, accumulate_algorithm=AccumulateAlgorithm.NAIVE, block_size=None, outer=None, carrier=None, tensor_scale_epilogue=False)[source]#

Build a QAffineFormats whose three Linear GEMMs are block GEMMs.

Each hook packs what it multiplies along the dimension it sums over, in the format of the tensor’s role:

  • The forward product x @ w^T packs the input along its features in input’s format, and the weight along its input features in weight’s.

  • The input gradient g @ w packs the output gradient along its features in grad’s format (input’s by default), and the weight along its output features.

  • The weight gradient g^T @ x packs both along the batch.

The arithmetic (acc, fused, rounding, the accumulate algorithm) is that of mptorch.quant.block_matmul() and is shared by the three passes. Results are in the carrier (float32, or float64 in binary64), stored in the input’s dtype.

A weight that arrives already packed, from weight_quant = BlockQuant(fmt, axis=1).pack, is used as it is. It is then packed once per optimizer step instead of in each hook (the memo sees the step’s in-place write), and in inference only once.

With square tiles (dataclasses.replace(fmt, block_rows=fmt.block_size), NVFP4’s 16 x 16 weights) the input gradient reads that packing transposed, so the forward and backward passes see the same quantized weight. A 1D or non-square weight format quantizes differently along the other axis. A weight packed in such a format therefore raises in the input gradient. To train with one, leave weight_quant unset.

For inference, mptorch.quant.QLinear.freeze_packed_() replaces the layer’s float weight by its codes in weight’s format, and the layer then holds only those (mptorch.quant.QPackedLinear).

Parameters:

  • input (BlockFormat | BlockQuant) – the input’s format (a BlockQuant names its rounding and tensor scale).

  • weight (BlockFormat | BlockQuant) – the weight’s.

  • grad (BlockFormat | BlockQuant | None) – the output gradient’s. Default: None, input’s.

  • acc (BinaryK | None) – the accumulate format. Default: None

  • fused (bool) – a fused multiply-add per step. Default: False

  • rounding (RoundMode) – the sum’s rounding mode. Default: RoundMode.RNE

  • accumulate_algorithm (AccumulateAlgorithm) – as for mptorch.quant.SplitMac. Default: AccumulateAlgorithm.NAIVE

  • block_size (int | None) – BLOCK’s and TREE’s. Default: None

  • outer (BinaryK | None) – BLOCK’s and TREE’s outer format. Default: None

  • carrier (dtype | None) – torch.float64 packs and multiplies in binary64 whatever the layer’s dtype, as for mptorch.quant.BlockMac (a BlockQuant that names its own carrier keeps it). Default: None, the layer’s: binary64 for a float64 layer, binary32 otherwise.

  • tensor_scale_epilogue (bool) – apply the operands’ per-tensor scales to each GEMM’s result rather than in the decode, as NVIDIA’s NVFP4 GEMMs do (mptorch.quant.block_matmul()). Default: False

Returns:

with the three math hooks set and every *_quant slot left None.

Return type:

QAffineFormats

Example:

>>> import dataclasses, torch
>>> from mptorch import BinaryK, NVFP4
>>> from mptorch.quant import BlockQuant, QLinear, block_gemm_formats
>>> w16 = dataclasses.replace(NVFP4, block_rows=16)
>>> formats = block_gemm_formats(NVFP4, w16, acc=BinaryK(16, 11))
>>> formats.weight_quant = BlockQuant(w16, axis=1).pack
>>> layer = QLinear(64, 32, formats=formats)
>>> layer(torch.randn(8, 64)).sum().backward()
